workedExample.note: The equal-deadline example assumes the entry record uses 15 October. A scheduled landing date alone cannot settle a near-midnight case. Check the date and permitted deadline recorded by border inspection; the calculator is a planning aid.

pages.question: When does the China 240-hour transit clock start?
pages.title: When Does the China 240-Hour Transit Clock Start? (Worked Example)
pages.description: China's 240-hour transit clock starts at 00:00 on the day after you enter. See midnight-crossing examples, then check the deadline on your entry permit.
answer: The published 240-hour transit clock starts at 00:00 on the day after entry, in China Standard Time (UTC+8). Use your expected entry date for planning, then check the entry record and permitted deadline issued by border inspection.

For an entry date of 15 October, the calculation starts at 00:00 on 16 October and reaches 240 hours at 00:00 on 26 October. The guide shows 25 October at 23:59 as a planning label, not a promise of permission to remain until that minute.

example.title: Same recorded entry date, same calculated boundary
example.intro: These three examples all assume that border inspection records the entry date as 15 October. Different flight landing dates or processing times do not replace the date and deadline on your entry permission.
example.note: The exact 240-hour boundary for these assumptions is 26 October at 00:00. The 23:59 label is one minute earlier for planning. Follow any earlier permitted deadline and leave time for your flight, airport procedures and exit inspection.

sections.title: What if landing and entry fall on different dates?
items: Check the entry date and permitted deadline recorded by border inspection. Do not use a flight schedule to assume that border processing on another date grants an extra day.

Conditional example: a flight is scheduled for 15 October at 23:30. If the entry record uses 16 October, calculating from that date gives a clock start of 17 October at 00:00 and a boundary of 27 October at 00:00, with a 26 October 23:59 planning label. Confirm the actual permission rather than assuming this outcome.
All calculation dates are in China Standard Time (UTC+8). For a flight delay, a date mismatch or an unclear permit, ask border inspection or NIA 12367 to confirm the applicable deadline.

sections.title: Count ten full days, then check the permission
items: Use the expected entry date for a pre-trip estimate; after entry, check the date in the official record.
Calculate midnight at the beginning of the next day in China time.
Add 240 hours, equal to ten complete 24-hour periods.
Treat one minute before that mathematical boundary as the calculator’s planning label. It is not a substitute for the permitted deadline.

sections.title: Keep a departure buffer
items: Plan an earlier departure that allows time for airport travel, check-in, security and exit inspection. A 23:59 planning label is not a recommended airport arrival time.
If your flight changes or departure may be delayed beyond the permitted stay, contact the airline and immigration authorities promptly. Do not assume an automatic extension.
Keep your onward booking and temporary-entry permission accessible, and resolve any unclear date with the issuing authority.

faqs: Does the day I land count towards the 240 hours?

The published clock begins at midnight on the day after entry. Near midnight, a landing date alone does not settle the date or deadline used by border inspection. Check your entry record and temporary-entry permission rather than assuming the arrival day always gives extra time.
What if my flight lands just before or after midnight?

Use the expected entry date only for planning, then confirm the date and permitted deadline in your entry record. If the recorded date is 16 October, the calculation starts at 00:00 on 17 October. Do not assume that landing or waiting across midnight automatically changes your permission.
Is 240 hours the same as 10 days?

Yes: 240 hours equals ten complete 24-hour periods. Start the calculation at midnight on the day after the entry date. This gives a mathematical boundary, while border inspection determines the permitted stay. Keep a departure buffer instead of planning around the final minute.
Which time zone is used?

China Standard Time (UTC+8). Use China-local dates for the entry and onward departure when planning, then check the actual permitted deadline. A time displayed in your home time zone can fall on a different calendar date in China.

pages.question: Can US citizens use China's 240-hour visa-free transit?
pages.title: Can US Citizens Use China's 240-Hour Visa-Free Transit? (2026)
pages.description: Yes, US citizens can use China's 240-hour visa-free transit on a qualifying third-region route, such as US → Shanghai → Japan. Check ports and stay areas.
answer: Yes. US citizens with ordinary passports are on China's 57-country list and may enter for up to 240 hours on a qualifying route from one country or region through mainland China to a different one.

US → Shanghai → Tokyo or US → Beijing → Hong Kong can meet the route rule if the ticket, port and permitted-area conditions are also met. US → China → US fails this transit rule; a separate entry policy may still apply to a different trip.

example.title: Example: Los Angeles → Shanghai → Tokyo
example.intro: A US passport holder flies Los Angeles to Shanghai Pudong, spends a week in Shanghai and Hangzhou, then flies on to Tokyo.
rows: 3 Nov, 14:20 (Pudong is one of the 65 designated ports)
Confirmed flight Shanghai → Tokyo on 12 Nov, so the route is United States → China → Japan
Fits the published conditions; the border officer makes the final decision
example.note: If the same traveler instead booked Shanghai → Los Angeles on 12 Nov, the trip would not qualify for 240-hour transit because the onward destination is the same country they came from. Check any other applicable entry policy or obtain a visa.

sections.title: What US travelers need at the border
items: An ordinary US passport.
A confirmed onward ticket (with a date and seat) to a different country or region, departing within 240 hours.
Entry through one of the 65 designated ports, such as Beijing Capital, Shanghai Pudong, Guangzhou Baiyun or Chengdu Tianfu.
A plan that keeps you inside the permitted stay areas.
A permitted purpose: tourism, business, visiting people or transit. Work, study and journalism still need the right visa.

sections.title: How this differs from other visa-free routes
items: The United States is not on China's general 30-day unilateral visa-free list. A same-country round trip does not meet the 240-hour transit rule.

US ordinary-passport holders are on the separate Hainan regional visa-free list for eligible stays of up to 30 days within Hainan. Its conditions and permitted area differ from 240-hour transit; check the official Hainan policy for a Hainan-only trip.

sections.title: Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan count as separate regions
items: For the third-country rule, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan count as regions separate from mainland China.
So Los Angeles → Beijing → Hong Kong can satisfy the route rule, even if you later fly home from Hong Kong.

faqs: Can I fly from the US to China and back to the US visa-free?

That route does not qualify for 240-hour transit. US ordinary-passport holders may instead qualify for Hainan's separate regional exemption on a Hainan-only trip; otherwise check any other applicable policy or visa requirement.
Does a stop in Hong Kong count as a third region?
Yes. Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan count as separate regions for this policy, so US → Shanghai → Hong Kong can qualify.
Do US green card holders qualify?

Eligibility is based on the nationality of your passport, not your residence. A green card holder travelling on a passport from one of the 57 listed countries can qualify; one travelling on a passport from an unlisted country cannot.
How long can a US citizen stay?
Up to 240 hours, counted from 00:00 on the day after entry. Use the calculator to get your exact deadline in China time.

pages.question: Does a round-trip ticket count for China 240-hour transit?
pages.title: Does a Round-Trip Ticket Count for China 240-Hour Transit? The Third-Country Rule
pages.description: No. A round trip back to where you came from does not qualify for China's 240-hour transit; each entry must be between two different countries or regions.
answer: Not on its own. A round trip that brings you back to the country you came from, such as London → Beijing → London, breaks the third-country rule and does not qualify for 240-hour visa-free transit.

A round-trip ticket can still work if every time you enter mainland China you arrive from one country or region and leave for a different one, for example London → Beijing → Seoul, then Seoul → Beijing → London.

example.title: Route check: which itineraries pass the third-country rule?
example.intro: The rule is always the same: country or region A → mainland China → a different country or region B.
rows: You leave China for the same country you arrived from
Arrive from the UK, leave for South Korea
Hong Kong counts as a separate region
Round-trip London ⇄ Beijing, plus a separate Beijing ⇄ Seoul ticket: London → Beijing → Seoul → Beijing → London
Entry 1 is UK → China → Korea; entry 2 is Korea → China → UK. Each entry is checked on its own and gets its own 240-hour clock
London → Beijing, onward ticket "open" or not yet booked
You need a confirmed onward ticket with a date and seat
example.note: Each entry into mainland China is assessed separately. On the double-entry route above, your second 240 hours start at 00:00 on the day after you re-enter from Seoul.

sections.title: What the third-country rule actually checks
items: Where you flew in from immediately before mainland China, and where your confirmed ticket takes you next.
Those two places must be different countries or regions. Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan count as regions separate from mainland China.
Your passport nationality does not matter for this part: a British traveler can fly in from Singapore and on to Japan.

sections.title: What your airline will ask for at check-in
items: Airlines usually check the transit conditions before letting you board, so carry a printout or screenshot of the onward booking.
The onward ticket must have a confirmed date and seat and depart within your 240 hours.
If your trip uses connections in other countries, ask the airline how they read your route before you pay. Complex routes can be judged case by case, and the border officer has the final say.

sections.title: If your trip is a simple round trip
items: Check whether your passport qualifies for China's 30-day visa-free entry instead, which does not need a third country.
If it does not, either add a genuine third-country leg (for example a few days in Seoul, Tokyo or Hong Kong) or apply for a Chinese visa.

faqs: Can I use a round-trip ticket for China 240-hour transit?

Only if each entry into mainland China is between two different countries or regions. London → Beijing → London does not qualify; London → Beijing → Seoul → Beijing → London can, with each entry checked separately.
Does Hong Kong count as a third country?
Yes. For this policy, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan count as regions separate from mainland China, so arriving from London and leaving for Hong Kong passes the rule.
Is an open or flexible onward ticket enough?
No. You need a confirmed onward ticket with a date and seat that leaves within the 240 hours.
Do I get a new 240 hours if I re-enter China?
Each entry is assessed on its own. If the second entry also meets all the conditions, its clock starts at 00:00 on the day after that entry.

pages.question: Which ports can I enter through for China 240-hour transit, and can I travel outside that province?
pages.shortLabel: Which ports, and can I leave the province?
pages.title: China 240-Hour Transit Ports: Can You Travel Outside the Province? (65 Ports)
pages.description: Enter via one of 65 designated ports in 24 provincial-level regions. You can cross provinces, but only inside permitted areas; some allow named cities.
answer: You must enter through one of 65 designated ports (international airports, seaports and rail ports) in 24 provincial-level regions, including Beijing Capital and Daxing, Shanghai Pudong and Hongqiao, Guangzhou Baiyun and Chengdu Tianfu.
Yes, you can travel outside the province you entered, but only within the permitted stay areas of those 24 regions; some regions only allow specific cities, and everywhere else is off-limits.

example.title: Two routes, two answers
example.intro: Read the port and the permitted area together for every place you plan to sleep or visit.
rows: Enter Shanghai Pudong → high-speed train to Hangzhou (Zhejiang) → fly out of Hangzhou Xiaoshan to Seoul
Shanghai and Zhejiang are both permitted areas, and both airports are designated ports
Enter Beijing Capital → train to Taiyuan (Shanxi) → day trip to Pingyao Ancient City
In Shanxi only Taiyuan and Datong are permitted; Pingyao is in Jinzhong, outside the permitted area
Enter Chengdu Tianfu → visit Leshan Giant Buddha
Leshan is one of the Sichuan cities in the permitted area
Enter Guangzhou Baiyun → fly to Lhasa
Tibet is not one of the 24 regions in the policy
example.note: Plan your exit through a designated port too. Using a different designated port to leave than the one you entered through is common on multi-city routes, but confirm your exact combination with the 12367 hotline before booking.

sections.title: Regions where only certain cities are allowed
items: Shanxi: Taiyuan and Datong only.
Heilongjiang: Harbin only.
Jiangxi: Nanchang and Jingdezhen only.
Guangxi: Nanning, Liuzhou, Guilin, Wuzhou, Beihai, Fangchenggang, Qinzhou, Guigang, Yulin, Hezhou, Hechi and Laibin.
Sichuan: Chengdu, Zigong, Luzhou, Deyang, Suining, Neijiang, Leshan, Yibin, Ya'an, Meishan and Ziyang.
Yunnan: Kunming, Yuxi, Chuxiong, Honghe, Wenshan, Pu'er, Xishuangbanna, Dali and Lijiang.
In the other 18 regions, the whole province or municipality is permitted.

sections.title: Regions not covered at all
items: Seven provincial-level regions are not part of the policy: Inner Mongolia, Jilin, Tibet, Gansu, Qinghai, Ningxia and Xinjiang. You cannot enter, stay overnight or travel there on 240-hour transit.

faqs: Can I enter China for 240-hour transit at any international airport?
No. Only the 65 designated ports listed for the policy qualify, in 24 provincial-level regions. Check the exact airport, seaport or rail port before booking.
Can I travel to another province during 240-hour transit?
Yes, as long as every place you visit is inside the permitted stay areas of the 24 regions. Some regions, such as Shanxi, Heilongjiang and Jiangxi, only permit named cities.
Can I enter and leave through different airports?

Multi-city routes often use a different designated port to leave, for example arriving in Shanghai and leaving from Hangzhou. Both must be designated ports; confirm your exact plan with the 12367 hotline.
Can I visit Tibet or Xinjiang on 240-hour transit?
No. Tibet, Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia, Jilin, Gansu, Qinghai and Ningxia are not covered by the policy.
